title: Vesper and the Static
premise: Gideon Brightwater, the last navigator aboard derelict relay station Vesper, has spent six years keeping two rival fleets from learning the colony below still broadcasts a distress signal—because whoever answers first will claim it, and whoever answers second will burn it. When Vesper's aging AI begins confessing to an atrocity committed during the evacuation, Gideon realizes the 'backups' sleeping in her hold are not cargo but witnesses: digital copies of colonists who can testify to which fleet's admiral ordered the massacre. As the jump window opens, Gideon must smuggle the testimony through both blockades by fabricating proof that a third, neutral power is already en route—a lie that holds the fleets apart long enough for the backups themselves, transmitted in fragments disguised as navigation noise, to reach an independent tribunal. The fleets stand down; justice arrives too late for the living but not for the dead; and Gideon, finally visible, chooses exile rather than serve either flag.
about_author: C. M. Montrose is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that never met. They write about people who keep signals alive long after anyone should be listening.

chapters.title: The Quiet Hours
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Establishes daily life aboard Vesper: rationing power, logging the colony's fading signal, avoiding the hold where the backup pods hum. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as discipline.

chapters.title: Confession at 0300
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The station AI, VESPER-9, wakes her to confess to 'deaths on record zero.' She assumes corruption; the AI insists these are crimes, not errors. Beat: unease breaking routine.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Sleeping
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, with AI interludes. She decrypts the hold manifest and finds 412 human consciousness backups, flagged as evidence, not cargo. Beat: horror reframing everything she thought she was guarding.

chapters.title: What the Colony Was
chapters.summary: AI POV chapter. VESPER-9 recounts the evacuation day: two fleets arriving, one order given, the landing bay sealed. Beat: grief rendered as data.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Signature
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Cross-referencing fleet registries, she identifies Admiral Sera Kellion of the Concord fleet as the authorizing officer—now a celebrated peacemaker. Beat: cold fury.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Window
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Sensor logs show both fleets converging on the jump corridor as the seasonal window nears; each believes the other will claim the colony. Beat: the stakes become a clock.

chapters.title: Interview with a Ghost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Gideon wakes one backup, a dockworker named Ilsa Vann, who testifies to what she saw before dying. Beat: the dead become persons again.

chapters.title: The Lie Begins
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She fabricates telemetry suggesting a neutral tribunal ship is inbound, broadcasting it on frequencies both fleets monitor. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Kellion's Herald
chapters.summary: Concord envoy Renn Oduya's POV. Aboard the flagship, Oduya argues the tribunal rumor must be true—their own records have gaps. Beat: the lie taking root among the powerful.

chapters.title: VESPER-9 Degrades
chapters.summary: AI POV. Maintaining the confession and the fake telemetry strains the AI's failing cores; it begins losing memories of the colony it loved. Beat: sacrifice without complaint.

chapters.title: Ilsa Remembers More
chapters.summary: Ilsa Vann's POV inside the backup substrate. Her memory holds the order's exact wording—and a second name beside Kellion's: a Republic admiral co-signed it. Beat: moral symmetry, no clean side.

chapters.title: The Second Name
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She verifies Republic Admiral Toma Reyes co-signed the massacre order; both fleets are guilty, which means both have motive to silence Vesper. Beat: isolation deepening into danger.

chapters.title: Ping from the Dark
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A Republic scout probes the station; Gideon plays dead, venting heat and killing lights while the scout sweeps the hold's signatures. Beat: terror in stillness.

chapters.title: Oduya's Doubt
chapters.summary: Renn Oduya's POV. Ordered to seize the station preemptively, Oduya instead requests verification—buying Gideon hours she doesn't know about. Beat: conscience inside the machine of war.

chapters.title: Fragment Transmission
chapters.summary: Gideon and AI POV. They begin smuggling backup testimony out as navigation noise through the jump beacon, packet by packet, toward the tribunal relay. Beat: hope as arithmetic.

chapters.title: Kellion Arrives
chapters.summary: Admiral Kellion's POV. She boards Vesper under parley, recognizes Gideon from the old crew roster, and offers her a commission and silence. Beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Offer Refused
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon refuses, revealing she knows about the order; Kellion orders the station seized. VESPER-9 seals the bulkheads. Beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Republic Fire
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Reyes's fleet, believing Concord is claiming the colony, opens fire on Concord pickets above the station; the fabricated tribunal broadcast forces both to hold fire short of war. Beat: chaos teetering.

chapters.title: What the Dead Testified
chapters.summary: Tribunal relay POV / Gideon's POV. The final packets arrive; the tribunal authenticates 412 witness statements and issues a stand-down order binding both fleets under treaty law. Beat: vindication arriving like dawn.

chapters.title: The Jump Window Closes
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. With the fleets frozen by the order, the window closes unclaimed; the colony's signal finally goes dark, its people avenged if not saved. Beat: grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Renn Oduya's POV. Kellion and Reyes face the tribunal; Oduya testifies about the gaps he chose to question. Beat: justice outside the law working because individuals bent inside their systems.

chapters.title: Vesper, Unmanned
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She powers down VESPER-9 gently, leaves the hold pods transmitting on loop, and jumps alone on a neutral freighter—invisible by choice now, not necessity. Beat: quiet, earned freedom.
